author: Theodore J. Karamanski

rights_note: Cited in words only; nothing copied beyond short quoted fragments.

note: Fragments read: the Chicago Historical Society moved the figures to its North Side museum (in 1931, with chicagoandcook_2017_1812_massacre_site), parted from their base; in 1972 the Society added the subtitle 'The Potawatomi Rescue' to soften criticism of the work's imagery; in 1973 dozens of protesters objected to it ('Wounded Knee was a massacre too'); the Society gave the monument to the City of Chicago, which returned it to Pullman's old Prairie Avenue neighbourhood; the city later packed the statue up for a planned park and keeps it in storage.
what_it_supplies: the monument's later history: the 1931 move, the 1972 subtitle, the 1973 protest, the return to the Prairie Avenue district and the storage
what_it_does_not_supply: the monument's form or its stand in 1904
